messages.subject: SE in occupancy modelling
parts:
Dear All,

First I congratulate Chandler for creating this wonderful programme. I am using the it for estimating occupancy of the Kondana Soft-furred Rat (Millardia kondana), a Critically Endangered species of rat from India. I am using 4 site covariates and 2 survey covariate at 50 sites for occupancy modelling. I have constructed 46 models and they run smoothly except, those inducing date as covariate. One of which I posted below. I don't know but may be number sites or capture occasions (3) are not enough for this model, therefore generating large error for p(intercept). Please let me know is this SE impact the detection or occupancy probabilities considerably (what would be ideal range of SE in general in occupancy modelling)? I am thinking to drop the models with date as covariate from analysis (definitely loosing some valuable data), is it any way impact overall results? does dropping erroneous/uncertain models have any issues with philosophy of multimodel inferences?    

 occu(formula = ~obs + date ~ grass, data = sinh.sum)

Occupancy:
            Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    0.192 0.348  0.55   0.582
grass         -0.399 0.334 -1.20   0.232

Detection:

obs0           0.423 1.160  0.3644   0.716
obs1          -0.671 1.280 -0.5242   0.600

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] SE in occupancy modelling
parts:
Hi Sameer,

Thanks for the kind words, but a lot of other people deserve credit for unmarked. 

I'm guessing that your problem is due to the way you coded observer. In unmarked, you do not have to create dummy variables yourself; they will be created automatically from a factor. However, it's fine to do it yourself, but you need to be careful. In your case, I think you only have 2 observers (is that correct?) and so you need to either exclude the intercept or exclude one of the observers from the model. Here is a way to remove the intercept:

occu(~obs + date - 1 ~ grass, data = sinh.sum)

Richard
